text:
maria: Hey team — customer reports a sudden p99 token latency spike (~3.4s) starting 2026-02-18 11:18 UTC for requests from us-east. They attached a trace that shows an unexpected hop to eu-west before hitting the us-east model pool. Request ID: 0ab3f. Can we triage?

jordan: Can you paste the trace and the exact request headers please?

maria: Pasting the trace they provided (redacted IPs):

```
client -> lb-us-east -> proxy-123 (us-east)
proxy-123 -> edge-eu-west -> proxy-eu-01 -> model-us-east
```

And the request header snippet they sent: `X-Request-Id: 0ab3f`, `X-Region-Preference: us-east` (customer sets it).

alex: That path is odd — I don't see any reason for a eu-west edge to be in the path if the final model pool is us-east. Could be an egress selection/fallback at the edge or a DNS/anycast map issue. Any recent routing changes deployed?

sam: I pulled routing service logs for the time window. Looks like proxy-123 flagged a backend health glitch and applied `fallback_policy: cross_region` for ~12s, which routed to nearest healthy gateway (eu-west) and then back to model-us-east. That would explain the extra RTT.

ingrid: Did the proxy healthcheck flakiness correlate with backend CPU or a transient config push?

sam: There was a canary push 11:15 UTC to the prefix healthcheck logic (release 45.2) that tightened health thresholds. Canary impacted ~0.3% of proxies — proxy-123 was in the canary cohort. The stricter healthcheck marked one connection unhealthy and triggered the cross-region fallback.

jordan: Can we reproduce quickly? If we simulate a transient backend fail on a us-east proxy, do we see the cross-region fallback path?

alex: Quick repro steps I used locally:

1) start a small proxy instance with the canary healthcheck config
2) drop connection to model pool for 10s (`sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP`)
3) curl with region header: `curl -v -H "X-Region-Preference: us-east" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "X-Request-Id: repro-123"`

In my run the route went `client -> test-proxy -> edge-eu-west -> model-us-east`, with an extra 1500ms added.

maria: Good repro. Customer is asking for an ETA on a fix and whether we can avoid cross-region fallback for short flaps.

sam: Suggested fix: roll back the canary change immediately (it tightened health window too much), or patch fallback to prefer intra-region retries first before cross-region. I'll open a rollback PR and a follow-up to change fallback order.

oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0428. Paging eng-runtime oncall.

ingrid: Can you also check the routing memo so we can avoid flapping clients? Maybe add a short grace period (5s) before triggering cross-region.

sam: Agreed. Adding a 5s transient grace in proxy health logic as PR #789. Rolling rollback of 45.2 to canary cohort now — will monitor for spikes.

jordan: For the customer response: ask them to enable `X-Prefer-Local: true` temporarily (we have that header respect) and we can offer to pin their traffic to dedicated pool while we fix. Also share repro and timeline.

maria: I'll communicate that. Thanks — I'll update ACME with the workaround (pin + header) and let them know we're rolling back. Will follow up when canary is fully reverted. :thumbsup:

alex: Post-mortem action items: (1) revert canary release 45.2 healthcheck change, (2) add 5s grace for cross-region fallback, (3) add telemetry to flag proxies that hit cross-region fallback >1% in a minute.

maria: Noted. Closing the loop with customer now and will reopen if we see recurrence.
